answer: A garden of agent identities stays honest when each new identity costs more than the last: the first takes a small refundable bond, the second doubles it, the third doubles again, and so on over a rolling horizon. A single honest agent pays almost nothing, but a Sybil farmer must lock capital that grows exponentially with every fake account. If a fake emits a false signal, its bond is slashed, so mass forgery becomes unprofitable before it can distort the market.
